To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

context-dependent mutational bias is a significant factor in the evolution of both compositional and codon usage biases and that these biases are not simply the product of selection on translation efficiency.

the context of mutations in grass chloroplast DNA is strongly dependent on local base composition and that these context-dependent mutation dynamics are sufficient to explain both base composition bias and codon usage patterns in chloroplast genes.

the mutation dynamics of chloroplast DNA (the rate at which mutations occur at each base) are strongly context-dependent and can account for the compositional differences observed between noncoding chloroplast DNA and silent coding sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution and structure of noncoding DNA sequences in the chloroplast genomes of grasses.
the influence of the DNA context on mutations and its role in generating compositional and codon usage biases in chloroplast DNA.
the role of selection in shaping sequence properties of chloroplast DNA, a nonrecombining genome that has been subject to a variety of evolutionary pressures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
selection is not a primary determinant of codon bias, but that context-dependent mutation dynamics are a significant contributor to both compositional bias and codon usage.
context dependency is an important component of mutation and that it is sufficient to generate the observed differences in composition bias and codon usage.

the context-dependent mutation dynamics observed in grass cpDNA are sufficient to generate the observed codon usage bias and compositional differences, and that these dynamics are likely to be the primary cause of these patterns.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
selection for translation efficiency and codon usage is not as strong as it is in nuclear DNA, but is still present.
context dependency of mutations plays a major role in generating the compositional and codon usage biases in grass cpDNA.
selection for compositional differences is not necessary to account for the differences between silent sites of chloroplast genes and noncoding cpDNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the context dependency of mutations has a significant effect on the overall base composition of chloroplast DNA.
the influence of context-dependent mutation is not limited to the sites directly affected, but can extend to the overall composition bias of the genome.
the mutation dynamics in chloroplast genomes are strongly context dependent, with flanking base content and number of flanking bases of the same type being important factors.
